content.text: {"headline":"Approve P2: targeted login-outage response, predicted 83.4% service level for 14:45-16:45 at ₹450 extra.","why":"General calls nearly doubled (124 vs 62.8 forecast at 14:30), driven mostly by login_issue calls (95 vs 39.5 expected), which points to a login or authentication failure. No incident ticket exists yet, so confidence is medium; ask IT to check logins now. P2 adds an IVR outage message for login_issue callers, moves 5 cross-skilled agents from payments to general (14:45-16:00), delays general breaks by 45 min and cancels general coaching 15:30-16:00. It is the cheapest plan that reaches the 80% target over the window: 83.4% overall, abandons 4.2% (vs 8.4% with no action), rest of day 90.3%. It breaks no policy rules.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) and P1 (no-cost) both miss the target at 73.1% and 72.4%. General would sit at only 57.0% and 59.2%.","P3 gets slightly better results (85.7%, general 80.4%, abandons 3.4%) but costs ₹1,260 vs ₹450 for P2.","P4 avoids customer-facing messaging but costs ₹1,800 and still misses the target at 78.8%.","Payments drops from 91.8% to 89.3% because of the agent move. That is a small, acceptable impact. General under P2 is 77.9%, just below 80% on its own, even though the overall figure meets target.","The outage message assumes a login failure. If IT finds no issue, the message could confuse callers and should be pulled."],"watch":"Check login_issue volume and general service level at each interval. Get IT to confirm or rule out a login outage, and remove the IVR message if they don't. If general stays well below 77.9% or payments falls under target, step up to P3 (overtime plus callback)."}
